title: Reconcile the authoritative source catalogue
scope: Every indexed module-source/interpreter/subject/kind mismatch and duplicate-source finding; all retained variants stay preserved.
acceptance: For each indexed finding, identify its retained declaration, actual implementation, owner and source hash; distinguish stale coordinates, missing content, deliberate historical evidence and real semantic gaps.
Restore or explicitly rebind actual implementation relationships with behavioral and negative witnesses. Do not manufacture placeholder files or remove historical declarations to silence findings.
Resolve the original finding or link it to a justified, explicit open obligation. Reclassification is not completion; unresolved authority routes to S1/S2.
nextAction: Start with Sourcery catalogue relationships reachable from the current runtime, then adjacent owners and historical/test-only records.

title: Complete runtime semantic and effect decomposition
scope: All 892 current runtime modules, the 336 bounded translations, 81 owner behavior specifications and seven declaration-only observations; the 565 SDK runtime libraries are included, not an additional count.
acceptance: Every runtime module has a reviewed disposition: generic mechanism, authored domain policy or thin effect adapter, with source/data paths and executable evidence. A custody label alone does not satisfy this gate.

Domain decisions execute authored semantics through genuinely reusable interpreters; demonstrate another authored policy/domain, changed authored inputs and invalid-input refusal without changing the interpreter.

Map each of the seven declaration-only observations to its actual obligation and either supply executable/effect evidence or preserve a justified declaration-only scope without representing it as generic behavior proof.
Preserve all retained specifications, amendments and cases; explicitly qualify any necessary semantic changes rather than silently editing expectations.
nextAction: Use authentication, authorization, credential/session lifecycle and effect ports as the first complete vertical slice; policy extraction alone is already qualified.

title: Close thin-boundary findings
scope: Every indexed thick-mjs finding, with the 296 Sourcery findings separately identified from the wider report.
acceptance: The existing goal audit reports thick-mjs=0 for Sourcery; handle all wider findings by their declared repository scope.
Extraction removes domain decisions from executable boundaries; splitting files solely to fall below a line/decision threshold is insufficient.
Preserve actual behavior and explicit effect ordering with focused subsystem evidence and managed integration qualification.

title: Close hidden-default findings
scope: Every indexed possible-hidden-default finding, including 348 Sourcery findings.
acceptance: The existing goal audit reports possible-hidden-default=0 for Sourcery; authored policy/data owns each domain fallback and missing policy has explicit semantics.
Classify harmless syntax separately with exact evidence, but do not treat a review note as removing an unchanged formal finding.

Do not weaken detectors, move defaults into another private JavaScript table, raise budgets or reset the residual ledger. Any measurement-policy correction requires its own reviewed, versioned change and fresh baseline, without claiming the former gate passed.

title: Pass the unchanged drift and architectural gates
scope: The 2,241 new findings, 1,157 metric regressions and all 13 formal goal requirements in the recorded audit. These counts overlap other indexes and are not additive tasks.
acceptance: checkPlatform reports pass=true, newFindings=0 and regressions=0 under the declared measurement policy; the complete goal audit reports complete=true.
Preserve the original residual evidence and criteria. New ceilings or broad acceptance entries cannot substitute for repair.
All seven report finding kinds have an explicit disposition; retain a crosswalk from this snapshot to resolved, superseded and still-open findings.

title: Define and enforce dynamic execution admission
scope: Every current dynamic/external/require boundary in boundary-index.json, preserving the 15 retained-site crosswalk.
acceptance: For every boundary, declare allowed source/package identity, target, caller, capabilities, invocation conditions, failure semantics and an explicit denied state.
Enforce that contract before execution, with allow/deny, substituted-source, malformed-input and lifecycle controls. A hash, custody record or passing import alone is insufficient.
Scope admission to the verified local host/profile. External/native operation remains gated by H1/H2; no blanket arbitrary-plugin or production grant.

title: Complete effect and environment custody
scope: All declared effect modules and environment inputs in the evidence manifest; current declaration coverage passes, runtime permission is separate.
acceptance: Every effect has explicit input/output schemas, source authority, capability owner, cancellation/disposal, persistence and error behavior.
Missing authority fails before effects; retries and recovery do not introduce undeclared writes or ambient configuration.
Keep unownedActiveSemanticMjs=0 and undeclared effects=0, refresh capability hashes and qualify controlled effect traces. Declared import coverage alone is not effect admission.

title: Resolve canonical Canvas schema authority
scope: Missing sdk/plugins/canvas/canvas-stdlib.rel; the derived 205-entry vocabulary catalogue is not its authoritative replacement.
acceptance: Locate and verify the authoritative source/history, or produce a specifically identified reconstitution with provenance, schema behavior, differences and remaining gaps.
Compare retained variants, consumer vocabulary/rendering behavior and migration rules; preserve all source evidence.

Record the canonical selection and its authority basis. Proceed under existing authorization where the source contract permits explicit reconstitution; request a decision only for an actual unresolved authority conflict. A local catalogue/test receipt alone is not canonical authority.
blockers: Authoritative schema/source selection is unresolved; a source-owner decision may be needed after the evidence packet is prepared.
nextAction: Inventory already searched locations and retained variants first; search only additional identified sources before preparing an explicit reconstitution proposal.

title: Close the two missing-history obligations
owner: Epistemic Core and Claimipedia Science source owners
scope: Epistemic 274a2a541789ee2e8b6576ec3aeb5d9651165338 and Science 647e065a69867ee767c5d9b7dac04bdce1946d19; current tested reconstitutions already exist.
acceptance: Audit the existing reconstitutions first. Close the already authorized identified-reconstitution route if its provenance, comparison limits and history-gap records satisfy the source contract; otherwise name the exact unmet requirement. Alternatively recover each exact commit and required object closure. Never claim exact recovery from a tested replacement.
Record searched backup/object-store/snapshot locations and results. Unlocated objects are not proof of impossibility; repeated local searches are not independent confirmations.
Preserve all branches, bundles, survivors and original Claimipedia overlays. Source-owner disposition is explicit; passing current application tests does not reconstruct lost history.
blockers: Additional backup/snapshot locations or access may require user input if exact objects are still required. Existing reconstitution is not assumed insufficient, nor is a fresh approval assumed mandatory.
nextAction: Audit the already identified and tested reconstitutions against the existing authorized alternative; do not repeat their implementation or invent another approval gate. Establish precisely whether any stricter historical requirement remains.

title: Verify the final native browser and workbench
scope: Final selected revision: reader/provenance, auth/session/CSRF, authored canvas, inspector/editor/history, publication/conflict persistence, reload and disposal/error paths.
acceptance: Resume computer use only on user instruction, then execute a finite interaction matrix with expected state, persisted state, network/effect observations and cleanup for every row.
Exercise valid and invalid interactions, canvas coordinate behavior, conflict reload, lifecycle disposal and publication refusals against the final assembled revision.
Capture native receipts/source identity and verify all temporary hosts stop. Older native evidence and Node/loopback tests are supporting evidence, not current native completion.
blockers: Computer use remains paused by explicit user instruction.

title: Qualify actual connector and host profiles
owner: PostgreSQL, Temple, package and host custodians
scope: The pg, terser, SQLite, Temple and caller-selected module/browser boundaries in boundary-index.json; qualify each intended host profile separately.
acceptance: For each boundary, name an actual supported host/version, pinned package/source, credentials/capabilities if needed and finite success/refusal/reconnect/disposal cases.

Use disposable local service profiles where supported; prove actual PostgreSQL operations and Temple snapshot/overlay loading rather than only stubs or imports. Distinguish local SQLite evidence already obtained from remaining host claims.

No access to production or third-party write targets is inferred. Unavailable/unconfigured profiles remain explicitly unqualified; remove an obligation only through an explicit scope decision, not a passing local mock.
blockers: Actual PostgreSQL/Temple target profiles, capabilities or credentials may be unavailable; browser interactions remain subject to H1's pause.

title: Establish runtime cache reproduction and active generation
scope: All three historically recorded runtime-cache generations; refresh current pointers, file identities and overlays before any retirement decision.
acceptance: Identify the actual current generation from the owning runtime/snapshot/profile configuration, not timestamps or directory order.
Regenerate each superseded candidate in an owned managed workspace from named source snapshots, databases, overlays and tooling; compare exact hashes or an explicitly specified semantic equivalence.
Produce a per-generation retain/archive/retire proposal with dependencies and restoration evidence. Unknown or unreproducible generations remain retained.
blockers: Recorded snapshot databases or overlay paths may no longer be accessible; no active-generation pointer was established by the historical audit.

title: Establish research-output reproduction
scope: output/; historical readable content was about 0.40 GiB with 37 denied paths, not a fresh current size claim.
acceptance: Refresh a non-traversing inventory, classify unreadable paths and identify each output family's source revision, inputs, seeds, tools and reproduction command.
Reproduce in owned bounded scratch and compare exact bytes or documented scientific invariants; record nondeterminism and all failures.
Unknown inputs, unreadable content or unproved reproduction imply retain. Engineering reproduction does not admit scientific conclusions.
blockers: Some source inputs or access to the historically denied paths may be unavailable.

title: Finish preservation-led consolidation
scope: Remaining redundant source/worktree/cache/output candidates; saturation-refresh remains registered at plan capture and historically holds ignored Context Hub state.
acceptance: Re-enumerate Git refs/worktrees and ignored operator state; preserve Context Hub state and previews with verified restoration evidence before retiring their checkout.
Require per-target source authority, byte/history preservation, demonstrated redundancy and explicit deletion scope. No general recursive cleanup or junction traversal.
Keep managed validation retention active and check scratch/lease release after failures as well as success. Protected recovery/source/history material is outside that retention policy.
blockers: Source/history and reproduction holds must close before their related copies can be retired.

title: Qualify one final integrated source revision
scope: One explicit committed source selection, all owner pins/overlays and the maintained managed profile.
acceptance: Keep all 424 bounded specifications and their evidence crosswalk; update hashes and expectations explicitly when behavior actually changes.

Run appropriate focused/source checks, then the managed runner for ordinary-copy assembly, Claimipedia/all consumers, runtime/semantic gates and both isolated bootstraps. Preserve every existing assertion; append genuinely needed checks.

Require exact profiled totals, zero failures/skips/cancellations, matching bootstrap identities, reader meaning preserved, post-run source/artifact byte checks, stopped readers and absent owned scratch/harness/lease.

title: Issue the final baseline certificate
scope: The complete five-area obligation set, all original goal invariants and final source/host identities.
acceptance: Every package has linked acceptance evidence and no unresolved required blocker. All original 13 formal goal requirements pass; additional source/host/reproducibility obligations also close.
Verify Git connectivity, bundles/refs, raw file identities, original user edits and consumer overlays; archive a bounded reproducible receipt with the actual final source/host scope.
Record what was recovered versus explicitly reconstituted and any accepted scope decision. Never substitute a certificate for absent history, native execution or scientific admission.
Only then mark the integrated platform baseline complete. Completion of this planning task does not complete that baseline.
